Subject: Production latency spike — SLA breach & credit request

Vanessa,

We experienced a critical degradation this morning in production between ~07:15–08:02 PST. Our monitoring shows: p95 latency jumped to 7.2s (our SLO is 300ms), error-rate peaked at ~15% for ~45m, and sustained throughput dropped by ~30% during the window. This has caused timeouts in our ingestion pipeline and multiple downstream retries.

This incident impacted customer-facing features for our onboarding flow. We need three things immediately:
- Executive attention and a remediation commitment (timeline and what will change operationally)
- A formal SLA credit for the breach and a clear calculation
- Post-incident RCA and evidence we can share with our internal compliance team

Please propose a time for an exec-level call today and confirm who will own the credit calculation. We will need documentation for our procurement and finance teams.

Thanks,
Nadia Khan
Head of Platform Reliability
Finos

Date: 2026-03-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — root cause & fix deployed

Team / Nadia (cc'd by Monica earlier) — short technical update:
- Root cause: an autoscaler configuration regression combined with a pathological request distribution caused resource starvation on our edge routing pool. The autoscaler failed to scale fast enough under a sudden burst of 512-token generation requests.
- Fix: rolled back the autoscaler setting and applied a hotfix to the scaling heuristics at 11:30 PST on 2026-03-02; we also tightened queue timeouts to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Result: by 11:47 PST p95 returned to baseline and error rates dropped to <0.5%.
- Next: we will run a full sweep of the autoscaler metrics and add an additional canary to the rollout pipeline to prevent recurrence.

Attached: debug_log_autoscaler_0302.txt (extracted traces and timestamps)

-Markus

- We should offer a short-term remediation commitment (timeline + SLO monitoring report) and follow with a contractual amendment if Finos wants the credit documented in the agreement.

Subject: Follow-up: remediation plan and proposed credit (next steps)

Hi Nadia / Carlos —

First, I'm very sorry again for the disruption on March 1. Thank you for flagging this quickly and for your patience while our teams investigated. Below is a consolidated summary and our immediate proposal.

What happened (high level)
- Impact window: 07:12–08:05 PST on 2026-03-01.
- Observed: p95 latency up to 7.2s, peak 5xx error-rate ~15%, throughput drop ~30%.

What we did
- Engineers identified an autoscaler regression and deployed a hotfix on 2026-03-02 (11:30 PST).
- Rolling restarts and queue-timeout tightening restored normal service by 11:47 PST on 03/02.
- We have added an extra canary to the autoscaler rollout and will run a targeted stress test during the next maintenance window.

Proposed remediation & monitoring
- Short-term: weekly SLO reports for 6 weeks showing p95, error-rate, and queue latency for Finos routes.
- Medium-term: autoscaler heuristics review and additional circuit-breaker protections by 2026-03-20.

Proposed credit (subject to final review by legal)
- As a gesture of goodwill, Redwood proposes a one-time credit equal to two weeks of average weekly usage for Finos (capped at $25,000). I've attached a preliminary calculation spreadsheet (proposed_credit_calc_0303.xlsx) for your review.
- Stephanie in Legal has reviewed the language and will prepare amendment/redline if you accept the credit and want it documented in the contract.

Next steps / ask of Finos
- Please confirm whether the proposed credit amount is acceptable.
- Would 09:00 PST on 2026-03-04 work for a 30-minute call with our CTO (Markus) and Head of Support (Monica)? Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210

Again, sincere apologies. We value our partnership and want to make this right. If you prefer, we can have Stephanie or Rishi join the call to discuss contractual language.

Best regards,
